analysis.title: Cross-Asset Spotlight: Yields Rise, Gold Falls
key_insights: In the week to Nov 13, the UST 10Y yield rose 28bps to 5.14%, USD/JPY breached 160 intraday, the Hang Seng fell 3.4% and gold fell 4.6%.
MS G10 rates strategists expect the curve to bear flatten in Q1 2027. They see the 10Y UST yield at 5.05% mid-year and 5.00% at end-2027.
MS G10 FX strategists expect modest USD strength, buoyant risk appetite and adverse terms of trade to weigh on the JPY. They see USD/JPY at 162 by 4Q27.
MS China equity strategists are neutral at the index level and prefer A-shares over offshore Chinese equities.
MS commodity strategists keep gold as their top pick, citing strong central bank and ETF demand among several potential drivers.
Weekly cross-asset moves: Topix +6.3% (a +2.6SD move), MSCI China -4.6% against MSCI ACWI +2.5%, energy +3.5% led equity sectors and materials -0.4% led losses.
The US Treasury curve bear-flattened last week, with US 2Y and US 10Y yields moving +2.8SD and +2.4SD. CHF fell 2.2% against the USD and DXY rose 1.1%.
Gold's -4.6% move was a -2.1SD move and underperformed the BCOMSP commodity index (-0.8%). US and European corporate credit broadly tightened.
MS Q4 2027 base-case forecasts: S&P 500 8,700 (bear 6,000, bull 10,000) from 7,562 on Nov 13. UST 10Y 5.00%, gold $5,250 and Brent $75.
MS base-case return-to-risk ranks gold highest (1.75) among the asset classes in its forecast table. Brent (-0.16) and copper (-0.22) rank lowest.
ICI data shows US equity funds with outflows over 4 and 13 weeks, while bond funds took inflows over the same horizons and money market funds had a small 1-week outflow.

The COVA diversifier screen ranks short copper and long consumer staples vs the market highest (overall score 84 each). Long energy vs market, short consumer discretionary vs market and short UST 10y rank lowest.

macro_indicators.interpretation: MS G10 rates strategists see yields staying near current levels, with the curve bear flattening in Q1 2027.
MS base case is only a small decline from the 5.14% level of Nov 13.
MS expects further JPY weakness after USD/JPY broke above 160 intraday.

risk_factors: Rising yields and a stronger USD pressured gold, with a -2.1SD weekly move.
A 28bps weekly rise in the 10Y UST yield to 5.14% was a +2.4SD move.
charts_described: Exhibit 2 plots the UST 10Y yield from Jul-26 to Nov-26, ending at 5.14% (+28bp).
Exhibit 3 plots USD/JPY from Aug-26 to Nov-26, ending at 160.19.
Exhibit 5 plots gold from Jul-26 to Nov-26, ending at $3,884/oz (-4.6%).
vol_and_positioning: MS Market Sentiment Indicator aggregates survey, positioning, volatility and momentum data into a risk-on/risk-off signal. CFTC data is lagged by one week due to the US holiday.
The COVA screen lists long vol in Russell 2000, US HY and S&P 500 among top diversifiers (overall scores 78, 77 and 77).
Positioning exhibits flag extreme CFTC net long and short readings beyond 1.5 standard deviations, but the text gives no specific names.
